questions.question: What is a goal? Distinguish between short-term and long-term goals with an example of each.
questions.expected_answer: A goal is a specific result a person or business plans to achieve. Short-term: achievable in days, weeks or months, e.g. sell 100 muffins on Entrepreneur's Day, save R200 this term. Long-term: takes years, e.g. pass matric, qualify as an electrician, grow a business to ten employees.

questions.question: Explain each letter of SMARTER.
questions.expected_answer: Specific (clear what is to be achieved); Measurable (progress can be measured); Achievable (realistic with available resources); Relevant (matters and fits the bigger purpose); Time-bound (has a deadline); Evaluated (progress checked along the way); Reviewed/re-adjusted (results reviewed afterwards and plans updated).

questions.question: Rewrite 'I want to save money' as a SMARTER goal and give two steps of an action plan.
questions.expected_answer: E.g. 'I will save R300 by 30 November for a school bag by putting R25 of my pocket money into my savings account every week, checking my balance every month-end and reviewing in December.' Steps: open/confirm savings account by Friday; deposit R25 every Monday; track in a notebook.
